title: A session-time lore producer leaves cache generation directories without the owner write bit, so the owner cannot delete the checkout
description: FILED, NOT BUILT. Relayed by team-lead 2026-10-13; opum-doc ruled under DEC-183 (g) that this rides behind the v0.14.0 pair (constitution Article 3), so it is not in LCLI-714. FINDING: a session-time lore producer writes cache generation directories without the u+w bit inside whatever checkout a Claude session starts in, and the owner then cannot delete that checkout. MEASURED 2026-10-13 by opum-desktop in its DEC-183 reader worktree .claude/worktrees/review-36 (a relayed measurement, not re-resolved here): .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations/8ab4c4c5.../ has mode dr-xr-xr-x and holds projection.lbdb (r--r--r--) and index.json (r--------). It was created at 14:26 local by the reader session itself; nothing ran in the worktree before the spawn. git worktree remove then failed with Permission denied after partially deleting the tree; the same happened earlier with review-28 and review-31. opum-workflow 0.15.8 session-start.sh and session-end.sh do not invoke lore, so the opum-lore plugin session module (or a lore CLI call it makes) is the likely producer, UNVERIFIED. QUESTIONS THIS TASK ANSWERS: (1) which code path produces the generation directories at session time, and with what modes; (2) are the read-only bits deliberate (immutable generations)? PENDING DESIGN QUESTION, for opum-doc: do not pick a fix. Candidate (a): generations stay read-only and lore exposes a supported cleanup. Candidate (b): a reviewer session skips the cache. Related prior knowledge: ladybug directories are read-only in test fixtures and need chmod before rm (see the fixture scaffolding note).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The code path that creates a generation directory at session time is identified, with the modes it sets, and the finding is recorded on this task

The task records whether the read-only modes are deliberate, citing the code: the immutability of the FILES (database 0444, manifest 0400) is deliberate and kept, and the directory write-bit test was itself a deliberate integrity check that DEC-281 (a3) withdraws
opum-doc design ruling recorded before any code changes: DEC-281 reversed the A/B choice as neither A nor B, and (a3) restored option C and directed this build

A checkout whose session created a generation can be removed by its owner: measured before and after with plain rm -rf as the owner (0555 fails with Permission denied; 0755 succeeds and the directory is gone). git worktree remove itself could not be run from this session because DEC-158 refuses git worktree operations outside the repository roots; the gating permission is the same directory write bit

plan: 1. Record DEC-281 (a3) verbatim on the record.
2. Publish the generation directory at 0755; keep database 0444 and manifest 0400.
3. Drop the inspector directory write-bit test; keep the file immutability tests.
4. Add the manifest file-set check against the directory entries.
5. Tests: fresh-tree rm -rf works; writable database or manifest still corrupt; an old 0555 generation still reads valid.
6. Mutation per rule: restore the directory test (fresh-tree proof reds); drop a file test (writable-file proof reds).
7. Before/after reproduction of git worktree remove.
8. File the gate-hole task; push and stop at a green head for DEC-183 review.
implementationNotes: DEC-281 (a1), ODOC-608 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T22:49:37Z): option C was reversed. Generation directories stay 0555 and the inspector's immutability check stays as written, because C would have changed a deliberate integrity check. The incident's cause is already fixed, since LCLI-705 gates the pane producer from 0.14.0, and the review-36 observation of 2026-10-13 predates the 0.14.0 bump of 2026-10-19, so it ran 0.13.x or older. The remaining case has a supported path, lore cache clear (LCLI-740), shipping in the next pair release, after which DEC-208's worktree hold lifts. DEC-281 (a2), ODOC-608, opum-ai/opum-doc#1776 (2026-11-18T22:51:24Z): LCLI-718 is REOPENED on the specimen below. lore-cli keeps this record OPEN and did not close it. Next is a measurement only: name the producer in review worktrees (the assignment prepare's lore agent context, the tracker-write hook's lore check, or another caller), and report it. Then opum-doc rules the shape: either C (directory 0755, immutability checked on the files, dropping the line-813 directory test) or stopping that caller from writing a cache in a review worktree. Until then the inspector check stays as it is. SPECIMEN: .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations in opum-desktop worktree review-125-3ae5ee2, created 2026-10-21 11:49. Modes measured: generations/ 0700, the generation directory 0555, index.json 0400, projection.lbdb 0444. Its control manifest records loreVersion 0.14.1 and exporterVersion 0.14.1, so the defect reproduced on a 0.14.0-or-later lore, which matches (a2)'s concern. MEASUREMENTS: the publish path is src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts lines 330, 371 and 373, reached through reconcileLadybugProjection (line 174) from any retrieval command; the read-only bits are deliberate because the inspector classifies a writable generation as corrupt (lines 813-828). CARRY FROM LCLI-724 (closed as a duplicate of this record): (1) when git worktree remove fails with Permission denied, git worktree list no longer shows the path, so the leftover reads as clutter rather than as the residue of a command that half-succeeded; (2) the DEC-158 ownership guard refuses a session any write inside a worktree path, so even a session that knows about the leftover cannot chmod or rm it by hand. STATUS: open pending the producer measurement; the shape is not ruled (C or stop the caller). This is a ruling note, not activity (grooming ruling D2).

DEC-281 (a3), ODOC-609, 2026-11-18T22:56:51Z, VERBATIM: 'LCLI-718: neither A nor B. DEC-281 (a3) restores C and lore-cli builds it now, with no more measurement. Why the producer no longer decides it: two of the six post-update caches are Claude Code isolation worktrees (ward-cli agent-...). Running lore in a worktree is legitimate, and the harness removes its own worktrees without ever calling lore cache clear. So any lore run in a worktree must leave it deletable. Shape: - The generation directory is created 0755. Immutability lives on the files (database 0444, manifest 0400). - The inspector drops the :813-815 directory write-bit test and keeps the file tests. - Where the manifest lists the files, the inspector also checks that the set on disk matches. Proof, both ways: - A fresh tree is removed by plain rm -rf as its owner. - A writable database or manifest still classifies corrupt. - An old 0555 generation still reads valid and is not quarantined. Separate: lore-cli files the gate hole (!e.isInteractive || CLAUDECODE === 1) as its own task. (a1)'s keeping of the directory check is withdrawn.' Gate-hole task filed as LCLI-790. BUILT on branch fix/LCLI-718-generation-dir-writable: the publish chmod is 0755; the directory write-bit test is dropped from BOTH inspectors (inspectGeneration and the inspectFreshGeneration fast path, which is the one production actually uses and which would otherwise have silently lost the cache); both now check the directory file SET against the manifest (manifest name plus control.database.file). Tests: three fresh-tree/writable-file/old-0555 proofs plus a file-set test, in test/ladybug-lifecycle.test.ts; two existing directory-mode assertions updated (lifecycle, concurrency). MUTATIONS, each run and seen red: restoring the directory test in inspectGeneration made the fresh-tree proof report built instead of reused; dropping the manifest immutability test made the writable-manifest case classify reusable instead of corrupt. REPRODUCTION, before and after, in throwaway scratch repos: installed lore 0.14.1 created dr-xr-xr-x and a plain rm -rf failed with Permission denied on projection.lbdb and index.json; the patched source created drwxr-xr-x and the same rm -rf exited 0 with the directory gone. git worktree remove itself could not be exercised because DEC-158 refuses git worktree operations outside the repo roots; the gate is the same directory write permission the rm -rf proof exercises. GATES: targeted suites green (lifecycle 19, concurrency+cache-clear 43, indexed-retrieval 43); typecheck clean; full bun test 5415 pass, 3 skip, 4 fail, where 3 are the LCLI-614 real-quest race tests failing on the lore 0.15.0 / quest 0.14.1 pair probe (reproduced identically with the fix stashed, so pre-existing) and 1 is an agent-context-budget timing case that passes 37 of 37 alone.

DEC-282 (ODOC-610, opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z) also governs this change, and it governs the SHIP SET rather than the shape. Item 4 VERBATIM: 'LCLI-718 / DEC-281 (a3), already in build.' together with 'Items 1-4 ship together in the next lore/quest pair.' Which ruling binds what, stated plainly: DEC-281 (a3) (ODOC-609) governs the SHAPE built here (generation directory 0755, immutability on the files, the file-set check, the directory test withdrawn), and DEC-282 item 4 places that same work in the pair ship set alongside LCLI-791 (item 1), LCLI-792 (item 2) and LCLI-793 (item 3). The change answers to (a3) for what it does and to DEC-282 for when it ships.
